chose: collapse-on-scroll by scroll position: the collapsing head is an ordinary-flow child of the pane scrollport, the pinned head is sticky top-0 in the same scrollport
over: a JS headroom/scroll-direction hook (mantine useHeadroom / useScrollDirection) driving a height or translate animation
because: mantine's headroom and scroll-direction hooks read window.scrollY only, and every /household/* view scrolls an inner overflow-auto div, so neither applies without a reimplementation; animating the head's height from measured scroll direction also feeds back on itself (collapsing grows the scrollport, the browser clamps scrollTop at the bottom, the clamp reads as scroll-up, the head re-expands). Ordinary flow + sticky needs no listener, no state, and matches the ask verbatim: collapses to the top on scroll, reappears at the top of the page

chose: one Pane/PaneScroller/PaneHeader/PaneBody set in components/ui/pane.tsx, with every white head moved INSIDE the pane scrollport
over: leaving heads as flex-none siblings above the scroller and adding a collapse-only wrapper
because: a collapsing head has to be in the scrollport to scroll away, and a pinned head has to be in the same scrollport to take the top edge as the first one leaves; keeping some heads outside would fix DOM order (pinned above collapsing) and break the shopping list, where the title collapses and the add-item bar below it pins. Also collapsed the 4 hand-copied 'h-[calc(100svh-var(--header-height,4rem))]' columns into Pane

chose: publish a pinned PaneHeader's height as --pane-pinned-height on the scrollport; AisleGroup sticks at that offset
over: hardcoding the add-item bar's height in AisleGroup
a second sticky context or z-index-only fix
because: measured 1 instance that needs it (grep 'sticky top-0' under services/web/src: only components/grocery/AisleGroup.tsx sits in a scrollport with a pinned head), so this is a variable and a callback ref, not a layout system. Generalising AppShell's existing useHeaderHeightVar into lib/hooks/use-height-var.ts made it a shared hook rather than a second copy of the same ResizeObserver

chose: only the heads the request named collapse: randomizer controls, shopping-list title, recipe-box collections trigger. Plan header and recipe-box filter bar stay pinned
because: the prop is per-head on purpose and a pinned head is the no-behaviour-change default; the planner's week nav is needed mid-scroll, and the ledger search is the control the request explicitly wanted always visible

chose: below md the DOCUMENT scrolls on every /household/* view; from md up the pane scrollport stays
over: keeping inner scrollports at every width
document scroll at all widths (dropping the desktop master-detail dual scroll)
because: a phone shows one column anyway (collections tree, detail pane, planner aside are all md:/lg:), so the inner scrollport bought nothing there while costing the one thing a browser only does for document scroll: retracting its own toolbar. Desktop keeps panes because that is where two columns scroll independently

chose: scroll restoration measured as broken (shelf left at 900, returned at 0) even though scrollRestoration:true and history.scrollRestoration=='manual'
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes
Playwright's click() auto-scrolls its target into view, and the target was the FIRST ledger row, so the harness scrolled the window to 0 before the click and the router snapshotted 0 correctly
discriminatedBy: click a row already inside the viewport at offset 900 and re-read the restored offset

chose: the instrument: Playwright click() auto-scrolls its target into view
because: clicking a row already inside the viewport at offset 900 restored to exactly 900 on history back; the router had been snapshotting correctly all along

chose: the headroom subscription lives in a childless HeadroomProbe that writes --header-progress; everything that follows the header reads the CSS var
because: useWindowScroll setStates on every scroll event: in Header that re-renders the wordmark, timer indicator and user menu once per frame, in AppShell the whole route. A childless probe pays one null render per frame, and the header transform, every sticky pane head and the aisle rules follow a variable instead of React state, so they cost nothing at all

chose: the header slides by transform, and prefers-reduced-motion pins it open
because: document height is what a scroll position is measured against, so a height collapse moves the thing being measured and the reveal fights the finger; the shell's padding-top already reserves the height so a transform reflows nothing. Chrome that moves itself is what reduced-motion is asking us not to do — verified progress stays 1 under reducedMotion: reduce

chose: headroom on the app header only on app views; the landing and marketing pages keep the nav pinned
because: reported from /household, which is neither navless nor an app view: a sidebar-navved browsing surface where this bar IS the navigation, and navigation that moves on its own is a worse trade than the 80px it wins back. App views are where it pays — one column on a phone, and the head under it is already getting out of the way
the top nav must never move on any surface — the author's call after seeing it on the landing and the planner; the whole headroom mechanism is out, so there is no subscription left to place

chose: the app header never moves; only pane heads collapse
because: this bar is the app's navigation and its identity. What can leave is page furniture — the pane head — which goes without taking the way back with it. Removing the mechanism also removes --header-progress/--header-offset and the per-frame scroll subscription entirely

chose: dvh for the fill/minimum heights, svh kept for the fixed pane height at md+
over: dvh everywhere including the pane height
because: a page whose content lands between the small and large viewport is taller than 100svh so it does not scroll, but shorter than what a phone shows once Safari retracts its toolbar — the difference is a strip of bare canvas under the last row, which is the reported cutoff (measured: no clipping ancestor anywhere on that page, every one overflow:visible, so it was never a clip). dvh grows with the retraction. The md+ pane height stays svh because the document does not scroll there, so nothing retracts and a live unit would only invite a resize mid-gesture
